question: per-cycle relay reach of a die wire on M8/M9 with optimal repeaters (ASAP7 TT, T 833.333); is a 1.0-2.0 mm relay hop feasible?

method.model: self-pair hop: launch relay ETM (worst o bit, TT lib, ideal ck) -> via stack relay pin layer->M1 + 5 um M4 -> repeater #1 adjacent to the relay -> [via M1->Mx, d um Mx, via Mx->M1, repeater]* -> last <= d um Mx -> via Mx->relay pin layer -> capture relay ETM (worst setup bit). Wires = distributed RC ladders (<=10 um sections) with setRC.tcl per-layer R/C; vias lumped (set_layer_rc -via). Clock 833.333, uncertainty 150 = U 60 + SKEW 90 (die_reach_1016 formula). The 26Q3 OpenSTA in openroad/orfs:asap7lock applies the ETM min_clock_tree_path at capture (macro clock tree delay), which reproduces pair_check o = O - R, s = S + R (rly_266_SN o+s 328 ps here vs 337.5 in die_reach_1016).
method.sweep: layers M8, M9; BUFx8 / BUFx12f / BUFx16f; spacing 100,150,200,250,300,450,600,800,1000 um; L 200..3000 step 50; reach = first failing L interpolated (slack >= 0 for all shorter L). Delay calc arnoldi (headline) and dmp_ceff_elmore.
method.calibration: the same model on the 0.76 ps/um source config (M4/M5 avg RC, BUFx8 every 160 um) gives 0.6315 ps/um, i.e. 0.76 carries 1.20x margin. reach_um_calibrated multiplies the repeated-wire delay by 0.76/0.6315 = 1.203 (same margin as today's planning constant). M45 check rows reproduce die_reach_1016 within ~5-10% after calibration (e.g. rly_266_SN 477 vs 455, qfd_cst_n 465 vs 425, rlys_296 497 vs 446, hbfd_rly_48 452 vs 413-421).
method.slew_rule: liberty max_transition 320 ps: spacing >= 600 um gives 330-430 ps (illegal, and beyond table range); 800/1000 um give 550-1030 ps. Legal spacing <= ~450-500 um.
method.tools: tools/die_reach_m89/{gen.py,analyse.py,grt_case.py,write_json.py}; runs via ot-run (ot-agidock128 sweep, ot-pve1 GRT), scratch /srv/opentallas-scratch/claude/reach-m89-1022

grt_validation.case: placed die 1.6-1.9 mm, S81 dsfd_dvrlyh_276_NS relays, H hop (M8) + V hop (M9); GRT with M2-M7 capacity adjusted to 0 (pins lifted by vias), estimate_parasitics -global_routing (setRC.tcl), dmp_ceff_elmore
grt_validation.grt_stage: M8 BUFx12f 300 um stage 83 ps (0.277 ps/um), 33.6 fF wire+pin
grt_validation.verdict: GRT-routed slack matches the arnoldi model within 2.4 ps (dmp model is 15-20 ps optimistic); headline numbers use arnoldi

answer.ps_per_um: optimal repeaters: BUFx12f every 200-300 um -> 0.267-0.285 ps/um (M9 slightly better than M8); 450 um 0.30-0.32; 600 um 0.34-0.37 (slew-illegal); vs 0.76 for today's M4/M5 160 um assumption (0.63 measured by the same model)
answer.hop_1mm: FEASIBLE on all four dies on M8/M9 with BUFx12f every 200-300 um, even with the 1.20x calibration margin (worst: hbm hbfd_rly_48 1.00-1.01 mm calibrated, 1.18-1.23 mm model)
answer.hop_1p5mm: model-feasible for S81 dvrlyh_276 (1.80-1.83 mm), qwen_kv (1.44-1.50) and hbm rly_624 (1.41-1.46); calibrated only S81 dvrlyh_276 (1.50-1.53). Not for qwen_compute qfd_cst_n (1.26-1.27 model) or hbm rly_48 / S81 rly_266.
answer.hop_2mm: NOT feasible in one cycle on any die (best 1.83 mm model, S81 dvrlyh_276 on M9)
answer.caveat_block_crossing: repeaters must sit every <= ~450-500 um (slew 320 ps). A lane cannot cross a 1.5-3.5 mm hard block on M8/M9 unrepeated: block-edge-only relaying (1-3.5 mm unbuffered span) is slew-illegal (>=550 ps at 800 um, >1 ns at 1 mm). Crossing blocks needs repeater islands / feedthrough buffer sites inside the blocks (M1-M7 via access at <=450 um pitch) or blocks <= ~500 um between rows.
answer.relay_quality: reach is dominated by the relay launch ETM: dvrlyh_276 o_eff 136 ps -> 1.8 mm; rly_266 / hbfd_rly_48 / qfd_cst_n o_eff 197-231 ps -> 1.2-1.3 mm
